requirement: Rate-limit API callers with a token bucket stored in Redis so bursts are allowed up to a capacity and tokens refill over time.
skeleton: A TokenBucket class over a duck-typed Redis hash client with allow and retry_after methods and argument validation.
caption: A token-bucket rate limiter over a Redis hash, written in the standard library with math, time, typing Protocol and collections.abc and no third-party imports; the client is duck-typed to redis.Redis hmget, hset and expire. The constructor raises ValueError unless capacity is at least 1 and rate is positive. allow raises ValueError for a cost outside 1..capacity, refills by elapsed time clamped at zero and capped at capacity, spends when tokens are at least the cost, saves tokens and timestamp and sets a TTL of capacity over rate. The fixture asserts burst and refill, the capacity cap, exact balances, clock skew, the TTL and the ValueError cases.

constraints: Invalid capacity, rate or cost raises ValueError
A backwards clock never removes tokens
A request costing exactly the remaining tokens is allowed
Each bucket key gets a TTL of capacity divided by rate seconds

rationale.teaches: Clamp elapsed time at zero, cap refill at capacity, compare with >= and always refresh the key's TTL.
rationale.why: Token buckets overfill after idle periods, drain on clock skew or leak keys forever when edge cases are skipped.

ops.docstring: A token-bucket rate limiter whose state lives in a Redis hash.

ops.stmt: from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping, Sequence

candidates.why_wrong: Refill is not capped, so a long idle period allows an unbounded burst.
A clock moving backwards subtracts tokens from the bucket.
Spending exactly the remaining balance is refused.
No TTL is set, so idle bucket keys live in Redis forever.
A cost above capacity is silently denied forever instead of raising ValueError.
